BAIR at CoRL 2026

Berkeley AI Research Editors    Nov 9, 2026

The Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) takes place November 9–12, 2026, in Austin, Texas. BAIR faculty, postdocs and students will be presenting research at various sessions, including an Early Career Keynote from Professor Negar Mehr. See below for the full schedule of sessions with BAIR members, including papers co-authored with collaborators at other universities and companies.

rewritten:
Get ready for an exhilarating showcase of innovation as the Conference on Robot Learning (CoRL) rolls into Austin, Texas from November 9 to 12, 2026. Researchers from UC Berkeley's BAIR team will illuminate stages and session rooms with their cutting-edge insights across a variety of presentations—whether through enlightening keynotes like that of Professor Negar Mehr or collaborative papers crafted alongside academia and industry peers. With over thirty main-stage discussions interspersed with dynamic posters spotlighting late-breaking discoveries, attendees are in for a whirlwind tour through the future of robotics learning. Key highlights include specialized sessions each day covering everything from agentic planning techniques to humanoid navigation mastery—every segment punctuated by shared knowledge and discovery waiting just around every conference corner.

Presenting their latest work at the conference, a diverse group of researchers—including Marcel Torne and Chelsea Finn—delve into MEM: an innovative approach that enhances vision-language models with multi-scale embodied memory. Joining them in this groundbreaking effort are minds like Karl Pertsch and Sergey Levine, who aim to elevate how these systems interpret actions. Catch their insights during Poster Session I from 5:00 to 6:30 PM at Poster 42 in the JW Marriott.

Understanding how robots perform complex sequences has taken a leap forward thanks to the work of researchers Yixiao Wang, Cheng-En Wu, Lingfeng Sun, Pengcheng Wang, Xiang Ji, Boyuan Liang, Guojian Zhan, and Masayoshi Tomizuka. They delve into compositional generalization within sequential tasks in robotics. Their findings will be showcased at Poster Session I from 5:00 PM to 6:30 PM with Poster 115 at JW Marriott. Check out their paper for an in-depth exploration!

Title: Expanding Virtual Horizons for Robotic Adventurers

Authors Runhan Huang, Xiangcheng Zhang, Haoyu Chen, Yitong Li and their team—including esteemed researchers such as Yen-Jen Wang and Stefano Ermon—have embarked on a groundbreaking journey into the realm of virtual exploration. They’re exploring new methodologies to enhance how robotic agents navigate digital landscapes. This effort aims to broaden robots' abilities in learning from online environments more efficiently than ever before. Notable contributors like Travis Manderson and Dawn Song are collaborating closely with robotics visionaries Pieter Abbeel and Antonio Torralba to drive this innovative project forward.

The Griffin board 120 is all set for LBR #19 with a focus on the intriguing theme "Reconstruct, Practice, Go Real," which delves into self-guided improvement techniques for embodied agents.
